text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- The upper house of parliament voted against a public initiative which would ban genetic experiments in Switzerland. Swiss citizens will decide on this initiative sometime in 1998.
- London-based investment group Doughty Hanson to buy Swiss sanitary equipment maker Geberit for 1.8 billion Swiss francs.
- Swiss Walter Meier Holding reported a 1996 net profit of 1.1 million Swiss francs. In 1995, the company registered a 25.6 million franc loss.

- President of the Swiss Radical Democrats Franz Steinegger said in an interview that he 'more or less' agreed with Christoph Blocher's opinion on the Holocaust issue. However, Steinegger said that Switzerland as a state should make a contribution to the Holocaust memorial fund.
- Largest Swiss supermarket chain Migros registered a 1996 net profit of 258.4 million Swiss francs, down 5.9 percent compared to the previous year.
- Swiss textile machine manufacturer Saurer reported a 1996 net profit of 50 million Swiss francs. In 1995, the company registered a loss of 75 million francs.
- Jacqueline Fendt has been appointed new president for the Expo 2001, a nation-wide exposition held in year 2001.
